text:
O brothers living after us, do not close your merciful hearts, for if you pity our poor souls God will pity your eyes looking on us. Five or six hang here together; the flesh we fed at too much cost is long since gnawed and rotten, and we bones turn to ash and dust. Let none mock our misery: pray God absolve us all!

Do not disdain our cry, brothers, because justice put us to death. Understand not all know how to keep a serene spirit; forgive us now after death before the Virgin Mary's Son; seek that His grace not be denied and preserve us from infernal embers. We are dead; let none trouble us: pray God absolve us all!

Rain has strained and washed us; sun dried and blackened our trunks. Magpies and crows tore beard and brows and dug out our eyes. Never for an instant could we sit: here and there we swung at the wind's whim, dragged without cease, while birds pecked us more than sorghum. Let no one join our brotherhood: pray God absolve us all!

Prince Jesus, reigning over all, keep Hell from taking our souls: we have no business or debt in its mire. Men, this is no jest: pray God absolve us all!

translation.title: Villon's Epitaph
